messages.author: 129e07bdb789652f
messages.subject: Problem when creating a package
parts:
Hello,
Using RStudio, I'm doing a package using packrat.
Everything works fine until I build the package :

 -  my package is built in the packrat/lib/ folder, is it expected ?

 - then when I run packrat::restore(), I get the following error message :

Error: Unable to retrieve package records for the following packages:
- 'mypackage'

Thanks,

messages.author: ab0d2be2ea8dabe8
messages.subject: Re: Problem when creating a package
parts:
Good point -- it isn't immediately obvious, but I think one would want to install it into the private Packrat library, and then load it from there -- ie, if package development is going to live in the Packrat library, then we should ensure it's installed and used there.

On the flip side, we need some mechanism for telling Packrat that a package is ready to be 'released into the wild', since obviously the net result is a package that we want in the user library. Perhaps it should be installed into both places by default, even?

I think the tricky bit is differentiating between when we are:

    1. Installing and loading the package for development, and
    2. 'Releasing' the package so it can be used in non-Packrat R sessions.

Any thoughts?

messages.author: cd47ca3bbd96bb85
messages.subject: Re: Problem when creating a package
parts:
I am not sure which direction you are going with this, but our current approach to deployment is to copy over the entire packrat/lib onto the production server. Since most of our production applications are basically back ends to a shiny app, the only thing we had to do to make this work is have the shiny app add the correct project to libPaths before doing anything else. 

This setup is a little trickier for non-shiny R sessions. We have a utility that the user calls in lieu of 'library' which adds the project library to libPaths and then loads the library. This has been adequate for us since only devs are using R sessions.  

So, for us the desirable default behavior is to build the package into the packrat library and nowhere else. 

Cheers, 
Yasmin
